title: Add RAG agent quickstarts, tool-calling samples, and docs site updates
author: Asha Nambiar
description:
Motivation: Provide opinionated RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) agent templates and end-to-end quickstarts that demonstrate tool-calling + RAG workflows. This PR adds user-facing quickstarts, example agent code for tool calling, curated RAG templates, and updates the docs site with new walkthroughs and API snippets.

What this PR does: - Adds three quickstarts (python, typescript, and docker) that show how to wire up a retriever, configure the RAG agent, and enable tool-calling for external APIs. - Adds a set of RAG agent templates (summary, cite-sources, multi-step extraction) under templates/rag so customers can bootstrap production agents. - Adds tool-calling example implementations and stubbed HTTP tool adapters in redwood-examples to illustrate secure call patterns. - Updates the docs site (site/docs/agents and site/docs/quickstarts) with step-by-step guidance, expected costs/latency tradeoffs, and a troubleshooting section.

Checklist: - [x] Quickstart content authored and smoke-tested locally using the docs site dev server - [x] Examples added to redwood-examples with README and CI smoke tests - [x] RAG templates reviewed by Applied ML for best-practice prompts - [x] Docs site updated and spellchecked - [x] Addressed lint failures from CI

Testing notes: Local docs preview (mkdocs) used to confirm formatting and code blocks. Redwood-examples quickstart has a lightweight CI job that runs the python/ts flows against a local dev runtime (mocked retriever + instrumented tool adapter). Manual run-throughs done for both python and TS quickstarts to validate streaming + tool-calling flow.

Migration/compatibility: All changes are additive. Templates live under templates/rag and examples under redwood-examples/rag-agent. No runtime or API changes required.

References: Linear tickets ENG-4268 (RAG quickstarts), ENG-4292 (tool-calling examples), PM-792 (docs request).
